_readme: MARBLE MAZE LEVEL DATA -- the single source of truth for maze layouts.
JSON rather than a JS module deliberately: mazeGame.js fetches this (like
main.js already fetches /copy.json) and server.js will require() the SAME
file when Phase 3 adds payout validation. server.js is CommonJS and cannot
import an ES module, so any other format would mean hand-mirroring the
level table -- the exact drift CLAUDE.md warns about repeatedly, and here
it would mean the server validating a layout the player never played.
FORMATTING: keep each wall/hole on ONE line. This file is authored and read
by hand and is heading for ~50 levels; a formatter that expands every {x,z}
onto six lines turns one level into 150 and makes a diff unreadable.
UNITS are world units, the same ones world.js uses (MARBLE_R = 0.38).
The board lies in the XZ plane: +x is screen right, +z is screen DOWN
toward the player, +y is up out of the board. Origin is the board centre,
so a level of size {w, d} spans x in [-w/2, w/2] and z in [-d/2, d/2].
Keep levels within roughly +/-10 world units of the origin: the scene's
sun shadow frustum is sized for the game board and anything outside it
silently loses its shadows.
Levels are PORTRAIT-shaped (d > w) because the canvas backing store is a
fixed 768x1180 and the camera frames the whole level at once.
GEOMETRY
walls: axis-aligned boxes, {x, z} centre + {w, d} footprint. Height and
material come from the renderer, not the data -- a level author
is laying out a floor plan, not building meshes.
holes: {x, z, r}. Fall in and the level restarts from `start`.
start: {x, z} where the ball is placed (and replaced on every restart).
goal:  {x, z, r} -- reach it to clear the level.
The outer boundary is NOT authored as walls; the renderer builds it from
`size` so no level can be accidentally open at the edge.
minMs is the fastest a human could plausibly finish, used by Phase 3's
server-side validation to reject impossible times. It is a floor, not a
target; goldMs is the one players chase. Both are ignored in Phase 2.
THEME names a cosmetics.js COSMETICS.mazeTheme id and decides how the
level LOOKS -- floor, walls, ball, holes, goal ring, backdrop. Themes are
admin-authored (the admin console's Cosmetics editor) and never owned or
equipped by a player, so a level's look ships with the level itself. That
is what makes the two travel together in a quarterly drop: new levels
arrive with the theme they were designed against.
An unknown or missing theme id falls back to 'workshop' rather than
failing -- a level must never become unplayable because a theme was
renamed or an admin override was reset. test_maze_levels.js still rejects
one at author time, so nothing SHIPS relying on that fallback.
PAYOUTS live in this file for the same reason the layouts do: server.js
require()s it and the client fetches it, so the number the shop implies
and the number the server actually credits are one number, not two that
can drift. The SERVER is still the authority -- it reads this table
itself and ignores anything the client says about what a run was worth.
Payout is per WORLD, not per level, so a drop tunes one number rather
than fifty and no level can be mis-typed into paying ten times its
neighbours. A first clear pays byWorld[level.world]; the FIRST time a
level is cleared at gold pays a further goldBonusPct of that base, once
ever. Replays pay nothing -- the money supply per drop is therefore a
fixed, computable number, which is what makes a client-authoritative
mode survivable at all.
THE GOVERNING RULE for every future drop: a drop's level payouts should
total ~65% of the stock that drop puts in the shop (gold bonuses add 20%
on top, so a perfect player lands near 80%). Recompute it per drop --
levels and cosmetics ship together, and a drop that ships one without
the other breaks the ratio in a way that is painful to unwind.
MILESTONE: an optional {category, id} on a level. Clearing that level
for the first time GRANTS that cosmetic outright. Milestone items carry
no price and cannot be bought at any balance (cosmetics.js flags them
acquisition:'milestone'; both priceOf and the server's priceOfCosmetic
return null, and purchaseCosmetic refuses anything unpriced) -- they are
the one thing in the game money cannot get you.
